brief.prose: The station is two decks of one structure. The Hub Deck stands still and holds nothing down: the Visiting Berth Gallery along the hub cradles, the Pressure Lobby at the spoke ladder's hub end, the Dockmaster's Office with the sailing board, and Habitat Board Receiving, where the landers mate and the Belt's ice and concentrate are sold. The Drum Deck spins at a sixth of a g: Orbital Access Arrivals at the ladder's drum end, the Drum Concourse, the Registry Annex where export permits are stamped, the Clearing House Window, the Cabeus Exchange where lunar alloy and crated instrument boards are sold, the Victualling Office for reaction mass and stores, and the Cold Trap, the social room. A public stair runs a second spoke from the exchange to receiving. One restricted room, the Rim Service Spine, is staff-locked and hidden off receiving on the staff-lobby precedent; it holds the storefront items that back the counters and the dark desks where the houses' principals sit enabled:false until the faction cut binds them.

def.desc: A wire cage of lunar alloy stock in strapped billets, CABEUS WORKS: STOCK on its plate. The manifest clipped to it is the stock the exchange board sells from.
def.name: Cabeus Works stock cage

def.desc: A sealed cage of crated instrument boards under Registry permit sleeves, CRISIUM INSTRUMENTS: BONDED on its plate. Nothing leaves it without a stamped permit.
def.name: Crisium bonded cage

def.desc: An intake manifold of tagged valves and netted bins, HABITAT BOARD: INTAKE on its plate. Ice and carbon billet bought at receiving are entered here before the landers take them down.
def.name: Habitat Board intake manifold

def.desc: A stores locker of crew-day crates beside the reaction mass valve schedule, VICTUALLING: STORES on its plate. Its manifest is the count the counter sells from.
def.name: Victualling Office stores locker

ambience: The drum's bearing note drops half a tone as a lander mates at the hub, then climbs back.
Earth comes past the concourse viewports, blue and small, and goes.
A dropped stylus takes its time reaching the deck, and someone catches it on the way down.
The grow lamps over the hydroponic racks step down to their dusk setting.
The sailing board clicks over: a cradle goes from HELD to CLEARED, Titan beside it.
A pressure door cycles at the hub, and a breath of colder air comes along the spoke.
The polar Sun clears the basin rim, and a bar of hard light crosses the hub ports.
A clearing lamp blinks behind the window glass, then a whole row of them together.
Laughter in the Cold Trap carries a long way along the curve of the deck.
A stream of water from a drinking tap bends a finger's width in the spin before it lands.
A conservation notice on the concourse wall updates the carbon the loops recovered this cycle.
The lamps of Shackleton slide under the hub ports, and the yards' hooded slips trail after them.
def.name: Aitken Highport

theme.name: TacSim 2350: the Highport
theme.style_guide: Present tense, no second person, no named NPCs in a room desc. Each room is distinct in sound, light and smell before it is distinct in furniture. The Highport has two physics and says so (doc 10 §3: no artificial gravity beyond thrust and rotation): the hub stands still and holds nothing down, so the Hub Deck is handlines, hook pads and tether clips; the drum spins at the Moon's own sixth of a g, so the Drum Deck is long slow strides, slow pours and a floor that curves up ahead and behind. The Concord sounds institutional and old: seals, brass plates, Shackleton time, the Registry's patience, habitat discipline in every poster. The houses sound like houses: Cabeus and Crisium price lines, the Habitat Board's conservation slogans, permit sleeves. Power shows as paperwork, as hooded lamps in the yards' slips and as who may open the service hatch. Earth comes past the viewports once a turn and the basin wheels below. Desc length medium (60-120 words); details are one or two sentences, dry, with a fact in them. Exit aliases avoid the kernel words.

def.desc: The gallery runs the length of the hub's visiting cradles, a long tube with a port at every berth and a boarding collar under each port. Nothing turns here: the hub stands still, and beyond the far bulkhead the drum wheels past as a seam of moving light in the inspection slots. Handlines run the full length at shoulder height, and crews pull along them hand over hand. The polar Sun comes in low through the ports, skimming the basin rim far below. The air is cold and filtered and smells of lock grease. A sailing board lists each cradle and the hull in it. The pressure lobby is inward.

details.boarding collars: Each collar ends at a lock plate and a cycle counter. The collars are the station's; a ship's own lock is on the other side of the counter.
details.handlines: Braided line at shoulder height with a clip point every two metres. Traffic keeps to the right, and the sign says so in Concord typeface.
details.inspection slots: Narrow windows in the far bulkhead onto the bearing race where the drum meets the hub. The drum's inner face goes past in them at walking pace, lamp after lamp.
details.ports: Thick laminated glass with an Orbital Access inspection seal in each corner, dated. Beyond them the boarding collars, and far below the long rim of the South Pole-Aitken basin.
details.sailing board: Cradle by cradle: the hull, its registry, its agent of record, CLEARED or HELD. A docked hull's name lights when a pilot is aboard.

def.name: Visiting Berth Gallery
def.short_desc: A long weightless gallery along the hub's visiting cradles, handlines strung the length of it.

def.desc: A round chamber between two pressure doors, each with an Orbital Access seal on its frame and a cycle counter glowing above it. At the centre the spoke opens, a ladder well lit in green that runs out toward the drum; weight begins somewhere along it and not here, where everything floats. A rail of tether clips rings the well. A placard in Concord typeface gives the order of operations if the gallery door fails to seal, and a smaller one beside it reads COME UP THE SPOKE SLOWLY. The air is still, a little over-pressured, and smells of door grease. The berth gallery is outward and the dockmaster's office beside.

details.cycle counter: Six digits over each door. The gallery side runs well ahead of the inner side, because cargo comes and goes more than people do.
details.placard: IN THE EVENT OF SEAL FAILURE: do not open the inner door, clip on, wait. Initialled by three inspectors, the last one this month.
details.small placard: COME UP THE SPOKE SLOWLY, and the rest of the station's saying under it in smaller letters. Someone has added a tally of sprained ankles in pencil, and it is short.
details.spoke well: A ladder in a lit well with a handline beside the rungs, running from the hub out to the drum's arrivals hall. Weight comes on gradually along it, and the rungs are spaced closer at the drum end for that reason.

def.name: Pressure Lobby
def.short_desc: A round weightless chamber between two pressure doors, the spoke ladder's well at its centre.

def.desc: Arrivals is the first room in spin, and it is built for people who have just remembered they have weight: a padded floor, rails at waist height, benches facing a wall of Orbital Access placards. A sixth of a g holds everything down gently, and a dropped stylus falls slowly enough to catch. A viewport strip in the outer wall shows the lunar south wheeling past, crater rims and the black of the cold traps, and once a turn the blue crescent of Earth. The air is cool and filtered and smells faintly of new carpet. The spoke ladder comes in through the ceiling; the concourse and the registry annex open off the hall.

details.benches: Padded, bolted, low. Newcomers sit on them for a minute after the ladder, and nobody hurries them.
details.ladder foot: The spoke ladder ends in a railed well in the ceiling, its last rungs closest together. A sign at the foot reads WEIGHT RETURNS HERE.
details.placards: WELCOME TO THE CONCORD OF EARTH AND LUNA. Under it, the five pooled functions in a column, and under those the station's rules on tethers, spin and the spoke.
details.viewport strip: A band of glass at eye height in the outer wall. Because the drum turns, the view turns with it: basin, stars, Earth, basin.

def.name: Orbital Access Arrivals
def.short_desc: The first room in spin, padded and railed for people who have just remembered they have weight.

def.desc: The concourse is the drum's one wide hall, its floor curving gently up ahead and behind, so that the far end is always a little above eye level. Crews walk it in the long, slow strides of a sixth of a g, and newcomers bounce. The inner wall carries Orbital Access notices and Habitat Board conservation posters; the outer wall is viewports, and Earth comes past them once a turn. Hydroponic racks run down the middle under grow lamps, and the air is green and damp with them. Doors open to arrivals, the registry annex, the exchange and the victualling office.

details.conservation posters: EVERY GRAM COMES BACK. A Habitat Board poster showing the loop as a circle with one small arrow leaving it, labelled LOSS.
details.floor: The deck curves with the drum. A ball set down rolls a little to one side as it goes, because the drum turns under it.
details.hydroponic racks: Leaf crops and algae columns under grow lamps, tended by the Habitat Board. A tag on each rack gives the carbon it holds in the loop.
details.notices: Orbital Access notices in Concord typeface: berthing rules, the spoke's hours of maintenance, a list of ports a Dray may file for from this hub, Deimos and Titan.
details.viewports: Round, thick, a metre apart. Through them the lunar south goes past, and Earth once a turn.

def.name: Drum Concourse
def.short_desc: The drum's one wide hall, its floor curving up ahead and behind, hydroponic racks down the middle.

def.desc: The annex is quiet in the way of a building that expects to outlast its visitors: pale panelling, a long counter with numbered windows, and behind it racks of sealed registers on spun shelving. The Registry's seal is set into the wall above, smaller and older than the Concord's. A permit press stands at the end of the counter, where export permits are stamped onto crate manifests one at a time. The light is even and white, and the air smells of paper and warm toner. A brass plate names the annex as Luna's highport annex of the Registry, with the Ceres mirror beneath. Arrivals, the concourse and the clearing house window are each a door away.

details.brass plate: THE REGISTRY, HIGHPORT ANNEX, LUNA. Below it: MIRRORED AT CERES BY TREATY.
details.permit press: An export permit is Registry paper: a stamped sheet bound to a crate's manifest. The press counts its strokes, and the count is entered in a register at the end of every shift.
details.registers: Sealed volumes on rotating shelves, each spine dated. Claims, charters and licences, notarised, never granted; the Registry records what others grant.
details.seal: The Registry's seal, founded at Luna about 2140 as the notary of last resort for the habitats' claims. The Concord's seal hangs elsewhere in the station; this one is older, and the annex keeps it higher.

def.name: Registry Annex
def.short_desc: A quiet panelled annex of numbered windows, the Registry's seal above the counter.

def.desc: A single long window of glass faces a back room of racked machines, each with a lamp that blinks when a balance clears. On the near side stand a counter, two stools and a slot; on the far side clerks watch the lamps more than the customers. A board lists the hours the clearing runs and the houses it clears for, Belt houses among them, and a brass plate gives the Concordat's five pooled functions with currency clearing last. The room is warm with machine heat and smells of instrument dust and new carpet, which the Belt calls the smell of dry money. The registry annex and the exchange are each a door away.

details.board: Hours of clearing in Shackleton time, and the houses cleared: Concord houses, Ceres Clearing, Belt correspondents. Ceres Clearing's line has a small note beside it, OWES LUNA, in the clerks' own hand.
details.brass plate: THE CONCORDAT OF 2268: the Adaptation Fund, migration, orbital access and the fleet, the Registry, currency clearing. Five functions pooled, and nothing else.
details.machines: Racked clearing units behind the glass, one lamp to a balance. Every credit in the corridor clears through Luna sooner or later, and these lamps are where it does.
details.slot: A brass slot for paper instruments. Most business is by account now, and the slot is polished from habit.

def.name: Clearing House Window
def.short_desc: A long glass window onto racked clearing machines, a counter and a slot on the near side.

def.desc: The exchange is a broad spun room with its asks on one wall: Cabeus Works' alloy stock by the tonne and Crisium Instruments' crated boards by the tonne, each line with a quantity beside it that goes down. The opposite wall repeats the bids from receiving for anyone who will not take the stair. Sample billets of lunar alloy sit in a rack under the Cabeus line, grey and light in the hand, and a crate of boards stands open under Crisium's with its shock foam showing. A railed stair runs a spoke to receiving at the hub. The room smells of machine oil and foam. The concourse, the clearing house and the Cold Trap open off it.

details.ask board: LUNAR ALLOY STOCK, STRUCTURAL, and INSTRUMENT BOARDS, CRATED, each per tonne with the stock remaining. The figures are the houses' own and change when the houses say so.
details.open crate: Instrument boards from the chartered Earth-basin fabs, nested in shock foam. A chalked note on the lid: CUBES OUT BEFORE IT WEIGHS OUT.
details.permit label: Every Crisium crate carries a Registry export permit under a clear sleeve. No permit, no crate leaves the hub.
details.sample billets: Aluminium-titanium alloy from the Cabeus regolith lines, lighter than the ferrous stock Kasei rolls at Phobos. A card under them reads DENSE CARGO, PAIRS WITH BOARDS.
details.stair: A railed stair in a spoke, signed DOWN by the deck numbers though every step of it is a step out of weight.

def.name: Cabeus Exchange
def.short_desc: A broad spun trading room, the Cabeus and Crisium asks on one wall and the receiving bids on the other.

def.desc: Receiving is the hub's working end: a long hall where the Habitat Board's landers mate to a freight collar and the Belt's water ice and concentrate go aboard them in netted lots. A counter faces the collar with an assay rig and a manifest reader strapped to it, and a board above it lists what the Board and Cabeus Works buy and how much intake each has left. The air is cold and dry and smells of frost and hydraulic fluid; a lander's pumps knock somewhere beyond the collar. A railed stair runs a spoke to the exchange, the dockmaster's office is out, and a hatch in the far bulkhead is stencilled STATION SERVICE.

details.assay rig: Grade scales and a core sampler strapped to the counter so they do not drift. A lot is priced by the tonne of what the rig says, not what the seller says.
details.freight collar: A docking ring sized for a lunar lander, with netted lots staged against it. The landers take the ice down to Shackleton's loops and the concentrate to the Cabeus lines, and they do not come back up full.
details.intake board: WATER ICE and CARBON BILLET at the Habitat Board's bids per tonne and METAL CONCENTRATE at Cabeus Works', each with the intake left. The figures are the board's own and change when the houses say so.
details.service hatch: An alloy hatch with a card reader and no handle on this side. STATION SERVICE, ORBITAL ACCESS PERSONNEL ONLY.
details.stair: A railed stair in a spoke, signed by deck number: the Hub Deck is nought and the Drum Deck one. Weight comes on step by step toward the exchange.

def.name: Habitat Board Receiving
def.short_desc: A long weightless freight hall where the Habitat Board's landers mate to the hub.

def.desc: A stores counter stands under the Highport Victualling Office's board, crates of voyage provisions racked behind it by the crew-day and a bunkering panel beside the till that meters reaction mass out to the hub cradles. One price a line, posted and dated, and no haggling column. A cold-locker hums at the back, and the racks smell of cardboard and sweet protein bars. The counter is clean, the ledger open and the stamp on its chain. A card on the panel lists the fills a Dray takes for the Deimos and Titan passages, in crew-days and tonnes. The concourse is out; the Cold Trap is through the side door.

details.board: REACTION MASS per tonne, metered to the cradle; VOYAGE PROVISIONS per crew-day. Posted by the Highport Victualling Office, dated, and the only figures in the room.
details.bunkering panel: A meter and a valve schedule for every hub cradle. Reaction mass goes up the station's lines to the hull; nobody carries it.
details.crates: Sealed crew-day crates, four kilos a day: food, potable stores, scrubber cartridges. Packed under Habitat Board rules, so the wrappers come back.
details.fill card: DEIMOS, a week or two in a good season; TITAN, nearer two months in a good season, one soul and a full locker. The card says ASK THE DOCKMASTER under both.

def.name: Victualling Office
def.short_desc: A stores counter with ration crates racked behind it and a bunkering panel beside the till.

def.desc: The Cold Trap is named for the shadowed craters at the pole where ice has lain since before there were people to want it, and it keeps the joke cold: blue lamps, frosted tumblers, a bar of lunar basalt polished black. Tables stand on the drum's gentle curve, and drinks pour slowly in a sixth of a g, which the regulars watch the way other ports watch a fire. One corner table carries a small Tycho Mutual card and is seldom empty. The back wall is a noticeboard of crew wanted, berths shared and a Titan run seeking one hand. It smells of beer and cold stone. The exchange and the victualling office open off it.

details.bar: Lunar basalt from the basin rim, cut and polished. The top is cold to the touch whatever the room does.
details.corner table: A folded card, TYCHO MUTUAL ASSURANCE AND SALVAGE, and a ledger that never leaves the table. Luna's insurer underwrites most of what moves in the corridor, and its underwriters drink here.
details.noticeboard: CREW WANTED, DRAY, DEIMOS RUN; BERTH SHARED TO TITAN, ONE HAND ONLY. And a card in a neat hand: THE TERMINAL'S PRICES ARE AN HOUR OLD BEFORE THEY GET HERE.
details.pour: Beer leaves the tap slowly and bends a finger's width in the spin before it lands. The keeper allows for it without looking.
details.tumblers: Frosted glass, heavy-bottomed for the low weight. The Cold Trap's mark is etched on each: a crater rim with a single star of ice in its shadow.

def.name: The Cold Trap
def.short_desc: A blue-lit bar on the drum's curve, named for the shadowed craters at the pole.

def.desc: A cramped office where every surface is faced with hook pads, so that styluses, stamps and tea bulbs stay where they are put. The back wall is the sailing board: every hub cradle, its hull, CLEARED or HELD, and the next filed departure with its destination. A window gives onto the cradles and, beyond them on the same truss, the restricted slips of the lunar yards with their lamps hooded. The Orbital Access seal hangs over the desk on a tether. A clock reads Shackleton time and nothing else. The office smells of stamp ink and warm electronics. The pressure lobby is out, and receiving is through the inner door.

details.clock: Shackleton time, the Concord's own, kept by the seat below. No second clock; the office does not apologise for it.
details.passage card: Pinned beside the board: TITAN, ONE SOUL, THROTTLED. The dockmaster gives the throttle word at the desk.
details.sailing board: Cradle, hull, CLEARED or HELD, and the hour of the next filed departure. The destination column reads Deimos or Titan and nothing else, because those are the only ways a Dray leaves this port.
details.window: The hub cradles, and past them the yards' slips trailing on the same truss. Hulls lie in them under hooded lamps; the slips are Concord Fleet's and closed to the trade.

def.name: Dockmaster's Office
def.short_desc: A cramped weightless office with the sailing board on its back wall and the yards' slips in its window.

def.desc: A service trunk runs from the hub toward the drum's bearings, cable trays on every face and four wire cages strapped along it: Cabeus's stock, the Board's intake manifold, Crisium's bonded cage and the victualling stores. Each cage carries a manifest, and the manifests are the station's real stock, not the boards in the public rooms. At the inner end a glassed office holds four desks with dark terminals and nameplates turned face down. The bearing hum is loud and constant, and the air smells of lubricant and cold cable. ORBITAL ACCESS PERSONNEL is stencilled every ten metres. The receiving hatch is the way out.

details.bearings: The race where the drum turns on the hub, felt here as a hum in the cable trays. A maintenance log hangs by the access plate, every entry initialled.
details.cages: Four plates: CABEUS WORKS, STOCK; HABITAT BOARD, INTAKE; CRISIUM INSTRUMENTS, BONDED; VICTUALLING, STORES. Each manifest is signed by the house's clerk of record.
details.office: Four desks: Orbital Access's director, the Habitat Board's chair, Crisium's managing director and the Cabeus works director. The terminals are dark and the nameplates face down on purpose.

def.name: Rim Service Spine
def.short_desc: A weightless service trunk of cable trays and storefront cages, a glassed office at its inner end.

def.truth: The Lunar Habitat Board's ice bid is Concord Fleet bunkering a Belt Squadron rotation through the Board's books; the Chair of the Board signs for the Fleet.
